previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was readmitted with recurrent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and low-grade fever shortly after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. He has a complex history including HCV cirrhosis, hepatopulmonary syndrome on remodulin, and pancytopenia. On admission, he was started on IV antibiotics due to immunocompromise and concern for infection. Workup revealed no bacterial source; stool studies were negative, and imaging showed no evidence of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. A left lower lobe pneumonia was noted but remained asymptomatic. EGD and colonoscopy showed stable varices and portal gastropathy without acute pathology, and biopsies were non-diagnostic. His symptoms were attributed to medication effects (remodulin and doxycycline) and possible viral gastroenteritis. Doxycycline was discontinued per infectious disease. Pancytopenia was deemed chronic and due to splenic sequestration. He improved clinically, was weaned off IV antibiotics, and discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up in transplant clinic, where he was officially listed for liver transplantation.

discharge, he was doing well for ~1 month.

On ___ (four days prior to admission) he was seen in Pulmonary

___.  He reported increased bilateral lower extremity edema

abdominal distension.  He admitted to some dietary indiscretion 
of salty foods when he was visiting his mother on the ___ 
but overall had decreased appetite and PO intake.  He had 
elevated JVP and ___ edema.  His diuretic was changed from 
Furosemide 100mg PO QAM/80mg PO QPM to Torsemide 40mg PO BID; he 
feels that this has not made much of a difference in terms of 
diuresis.  

On the day of presentation, he went for outpatient TTE which 
showed RV pressure/volume overload but preserved RV function, 
hyperdynamic LV, moderate pulmonary artery systolic 
hypertension, and late agitated saline bubbles appearing in LA 
suggesting pulmonary arteriovenous shunting.  At the study, he 
was noted to be tachycardic and hypotensive with SBP ___ 
(baseline SBP ~110).  When he returned home, the Pulmonology 
Fellow called to discuss the TTE result and the patient reported 
lightheadedness.  In light of his new hypotension and his 
hypoxia in clinic, he was referred to the ED for CTA to rule out 
PE, as well as management of his volume overload.

In the ___ ED, initial VS were: T 98.2, HR 103, BP 107/56, RR 
24, POx 98% 4L NC.  Labs were notable for WBC 17.1 (92.2% N, 
note that he has usually been leukopenic).  UA negative and CXR 
clear.  Hct 31 (which is baseline), plt 16.  INR 1.3.  New 
hyponatremia with Na 129, bicarb 21, BUN/Cr ___ (baseline Cr 
0.7).  LFTs near recent prior with ALT 24, AST 54, AP 210, TBili 
1.9.  BNP 4366.  Lactate 2.2.  He underwent CTA which was 
nondiagnostic due to poor contrast bolus timing but no filling 
defect in main pulmonary arterial tree.  Scattered opacities in 
both lungs, calcified granuloma and lymph nodes c/w 
granulomatous infection.  There were initially plans for 
admission to Hepatology, but he triggered for hypotension to 
78/40.  There was concern for sepsis; he was given 3L normal 
saline and Vanc/Pip-Tazo.  Patient declined foley but urine 
output 200cc.  It was felt that repeat CXR suggested LLL 
infection.  Due to hypotension he was admitted to the MICU.  VS 
prior to transfer were: T 97.8, HR 98, BP 95/41, RR 18, POx 100% 
RA.

On arrival to the MICU, he feels quite well and says he is ""here 
entirely under the doctors' orders orders.""  When he is not 
exerting himself he has no dyspnea.  No difference in breathing 
comfort when he is lying down vs sitting up.  He does feel that 
his ___ is slightly bigger than his RLE.  In terms of infectious 
symptoms, he denies any fevers, chills, rhinorrhea, cough, sick 
contacts.  Generally has loose stools due to Lactulose but this 
has not been worse recently.  Mild abdominal tenderness but no 
pain.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ Year old male with HCV cirrhosis MELD 13 decompensated by HE, 
varices, ascites, and portopulmonary syndrome on chronic 
Remodulin infusion therapy and on transplant list who presents 
with hypotension and new hypoxemia and found to have 
Enterobacter bacteremia.

#. Hypotension: Likely ___ Enterobacter sepsis as it improved 
with antibiotic treatment and IVF. Patient with history of 
cirrhosis and has baseline SBP is 110 but he had been 
intermittently hypotensive to the 80's during his MICU course.  
His blood pressure remained in the ___ for the rest of his 
hospitalization in the setting of aggressive diuresis.  He 
remained asymptomatic throughout his ICU stay as well as after 
transfer to the floor.

# Hypoxemia - Pulmonary embolus was considered and evaluated 
for, however the bolus was poorly timed and this was not able to 
be officially ruled out.  ___ obtained and it was negative. 
Most likely etiolgy is pulmonary edema as he appeared volume 
overloaded on exam - lower extremity edema, bibasilar crackles, 
and elevated JVD and improved with diuresis. He was initially 
diuresed in the MICU and his oxygen was able to be weaned off 
(at baseline he requires 4L O2 NC only while sleeping). While on 
the floor, he was satting well >90% on room air. He was 
continued to be aggressively diuresed with IV lasix and 
metolazone. He was total net negative >8L and his weight 
decreased by about 14kg from admission. His labs were monitored 
BID and his potassium was aggressively repleted. He was 
transitioned back to his home torsemide at discharge. 
Pulmonology was following patient throughout hospitalization. He 
was continued on his treprostinil infusion and sildenafil TID. 
He had a right heart cath on ___ which showed mPAP of 25. At 
discharge, he was feeling well and was satting well on room air. 


# Enterobacter bacteremia - blood grew pansensitive enterobacter 
and he was started on cefepime IV. No clear source identified. 
Patient had transient mild periumbilical pain, but does not have 
much ascites on ultrasound (also would have been treated for SBP 
with the cefepime). His UA was negative and no sign of an acute 
infectious process on CXR and CT. No skin lesions or diarrhea. 
No vegetations seen on recent TTE. He does have a tunneled line 
for his treprostinil which could either be the source or act as 
a nidus for continued infection. However, since it was a low 
bacterial burden (one bottle) and patient remained 
hemodynamically stable and afebrile, the tunneled line was kept 
given that it was not feasible to remove and replace tunneled 
line given his continuous need for pulmonary vasodilators. At 
discharge, he was switched to oral cipro 500mg q12h to finish a 
2 week course (last day on ___. 

#. HCV cirrhosis: patient on transplant list. Cirrhosis has been 
complicated by prior HE, varices, ascites, thrombocytopenia, 
portopulmonary hypertension. MELD is 13, but given pulmonary 
symptoms, his mortality rate is higher. He was continued on his 
home dose of lactulose and rifaximin. Diuretics were handled as 
per above.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Hypotension, here to evaluate for evidence of volume overload.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable upright AP radiograph of the chest.

FINDINGS:  A right central venous catheter is unchanged in position with the
tip terminating at the cavoatrial junction.  Again noted are bibasilar
opacities on the left greater than the right.  No significant pleural effusion
or pneumothorax is detected.  The cardiac silhouette is top normal in size. 
The mediastinal and hilar contours are within normal limits.  The trachea is
midline.

IMPRESSION:  Stable appearance of the chest with left greater than right
bibasilar opacities.

INDICATION:  History of HCV cirrhosis, admitted with leukocytosis and
hypotension, here to evaluate for ascites.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal ultrasound last performed on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Targeted sonographic assessment of the abdomen was performed to
evaluate for the presence of ascites.

FINDINGS:  Targeted sonographic assessment in the four quadrants of the
abdomen reveal the presence of ascites with the largest pocket of fluid
located in the pelvis and around the liver in the right upper quadrant.  A
nodular contour of the liver is compatible with cirrhosis.  Splenomegaly is
also noted.

IMPRESSION:  Small amount of intra-abdominal ascites, predominantly within the
pelvic and perihepatic regions.

INDICATION:  Left lower extremity swelling greater than the right, here to
evaluate for deep venous thrombosis.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and color Doppler sonography was performed of the
bilateral common femoral, left superficial femoral, left popliteal, left
posterior tibial, and left peroneal veins.  All visualized venous structures
show normal compressibility, augmentation and flow.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of DVT in the left lower extremity.
